Please read the following multiple-choice questions and provide the most likely correct answer based on the options given.

Context: None

Question: Mr. Haskell has decided to buy a rental property. The building costs $50,000 and the land costs $30,000. The annual rent income is estimated to be $10,450 and the annual expense, $3,200. Mr. Haskell plans to depreciate the building by the straight line method over 40 years. Mr. Haskell wants to choose the best of three investment plans. Plan A Pay the full $80,000 from personal account. Plan B Borrow $30,000 and pay $50,000 from personal account. Rate of interest is 4(1/2)%. Plan C Borrow $60,000 and pay $20,000 from personal account. Rate of interest is 5 (1/4)%. If the tax rate is 40%, which investment plan has the highest rate of return?

Options: 
A. Plan B, if the interest rates drop to 3%
B. Plan A, if the tax rate decreases to 30%
C. Plan A
D. Plan C, assuming rental income increases by 5% annually
E. Plan C
F. None of the plans
G. Plan B
H. Plan C, if additional tax deductions are available for interest paid
I. Plan A, with a government grant covering 10% of the initial investment
J. Plan B, with an additional private investor contributing $10,000

Provide the correct letter choice in \boxed{X}, where X is the correct letter choice. Keep the explanation or feedback within 3 sentences.

    Alternatively, just compare the Effective After-Tax Yield.

    Let's calculate the **After-Tax Cash Flow (ATCF)** for each plan first.
    Formula: $ATCF = (\text{Rent} - \text{Cash Expenses} - \text{Tax Interest}) + (\text{Interest Rate} \times \text{Loan Amount})$.
    Wait, let's look at the tax bracket and deductions.
    Income to be taxed = Rent - Cash Expenses - Interest - Depreciation.
    Tax = $40\% \times (\text{Income} - \text{Interest} - \text{Depreciation})$.
    Net Income = $\text{Rental Income} - \text{Cash Expenses} - \text{Interest} - \text{Tax}$.
    Actually, the standard Operating Income (Net Operating Income, NOI) is Rent - Cash Expenses.
    NOI = $10,450 - $3,200 = $7,250.
    Taxable Income = NOI - Interest - Depreciation.
    Tax Savings from Depreciation (DIA) = $40\% \times D = $1,250 \times 0.4 = $500.
    Tax Savings from Interest (DIS) = $40\% \times I$.
    So, Tax Payable = $0.4 \times (\text{NOI} - \text{Interest})$.
    (Depreciation is a contra-item that reduces taxable income, taxes are 40% of taxable income).
    Wait, Tax Piability = $0.4 \times (7,250 - \text{Interest} - 1,250)$.
    Wait, Tax Piability = $0.4 \times (7,250 - \text{Interest} - 1,250)$.
    So Free Cash Flow (FCF) = NOI - Interest - Tax.
    Tax = $0.4 \times (NOI - Interest - Depreciation)$.
    FCF = NOI - Interest - $0.4 \times (NOI - Interest - Depreciation \text{)} = 0.6 \times \text{NOI} - 0.4 \times \text{Interest} + 0.4 \times \text{Depreciation}$.

    Let's calculate FCF for each option using the cost of capital.

    *Note on Initial Investment for Rate of Return:*
    We are comparing returns on the $80,000 total investment.
    Plan A: Cash Flow = FCF. Cost = $80,000.
    Plan B: Borrow $30,000 at 4.5%, Invest $50,000.
    Plan C: Borrow $60,000 at 5.25%, Invest $20,000.

    Depreciation = $1,250
    Remaining (Equity Earnings) = NOI - Interest - Tax.
    Taxable Income = NOI - Interest - Depreciation.
    Tax = $0.40 \times (7,250 - \text{Interest} - 1,250) = 0.4 \times (6,000 - \text{Interest})$.
    FCF = NOI - Interest - Tax
       = $7,250 - \text{Interest} - (2,400 - 0.4\text{Interest})$

    Cost = $80,000$.
